name: Device model and manufacturer
plain: Reads exact model and manufacturer on Android; iOS gives a model code via sysctl.
meaning: Tells price tier, age, and often region. It is the biggest single device-fingerprint field: Android has thousands of models, iPhone has about 40 live models.

android.api_surface: Build.MODEL, MANUFACTURER, BRAND, DEVICE, PRODUCT, HARDWARE
android.note: Free text, for example Pixel 9 Pro; about 10,000 distinct models in the wild

ios.api_surface: hw.machine is not in the Required Reason list; the marketing name needs a lookup table
ios.note: Marketing name not exposed; model identifier such as iPhone16,1 is

limits.headline: Can see your exact phone model and maker on Android, and a model code on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app can ask the moment it opens
can: See your exact Android model and brand, such as Pixel 9 Pro
See an iPhone model code, such as iPhone16,1
Pick layouts and fixes for your kind of phone
Tell your phone apart from one of about 10,000 Android models
cannot: Get the iPhone marketing name directly; the app must look up the code in its own table
Learn who you are from the model alone
Change the model or unlock hidden features
limits.differs: Android gives a readable model name. iPhone gives a code the app has to translate.

story.what_it_is: An app can read your exact phone model and maker.
story.for_you: You never see it. The model tells an app how new and costly your phone is, and often which country you live in. It is the biggest single detail used to tell phones apart.
story.for_makers: Makers fix bugs for one model and tune games to match. Ad and fraud tools use it as a main fingerprint field, since Android has thousands of models and iPhone about 40.

use_cases.example: A game applies special settings for one tablet model with a known graphics bug.
A store app shows premium offers to people on expensive phones.
A bank blocks a login where the model does not match what the account normally uses.
An advertiser targets accessories to people with one phone model.
A crash tool shows which models fail most, to guide testing.
A streaming app picks a video profile known to work on your model.

story.android_note: Exact model and maker are readable with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iOS gives a model code through system calls, like iPhone15,2, which maps to one model.

linkedin.how: Policy 1.5: LinkedIn receives network and device data including device identifier and features, IP address and operating system. Play Data safety lists crash logs, diagnostics and performance data.

refs.label: Kurtz et al.: Fingerprinting Mobile Devices Using Personalized Configurations (PoPETs 2016)
